title: Hearing the Kirby band without him at the Academy of Music
summary: In rain gear, stationed at 110th Street, he sat in the audience and found the band had lost its sound and precision, which depressed him.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Now, so when you left it was strictly to go into the service. That was --
And at that point the whole band just sort of collapsed, right? Disbanded.

Well, not all at once, because they played a theater down at 14th Street, the Academy of Music. Used to be a theater down -- they still had vaudeville, sort of. And there was a fellow named Johnson who took my place, so then he -- so then that was two of the group that were out, Billy Kyle and myself. And I remember I went down and I was stationed at 110th Street at that time, so I never will

forget, it was raining real hard that day, and for the first time I put on the rainwear that the Army gives you. You know, they give you the boots and the raincoat and the -- and I put them on that day and I went to hear the band. I didn't let them know, I just sat in the audience, you know, bought a ticket and sat in the audience, and they didn't sound nothing like the Kirby band. The sound wasn't there. The precision wasn't there, you know. And I was so depressed with what being in the Army and what was happening to the band, which I was so crazy, you know. It was just a terrible time.
Now, you say someone named Jones or Johnson?
I seem to remember that it was Clyde Hart, I think. I'm not -- it escapes me now, but I believe it was Clyde Hart.
Now, did you go backstage? Did you make your presence known?
Yes, I went backstage after. After. Because I didn't want them to know I was there before.
Yes, I went back and they all saw me
in my uniform and everything, you know, and I said, "Well, that's the way things happen."
